_comment: The files a new project needs to build CSG-in-Blender levels the way this repository does. scripts/copy_kit.py copies them with their provenance; --check proves every path still exists here.

files.why: Godot-to-Blender axes, preview materials, box and cylinder brushes with per-face materials, world-aligned UVs (live Geometry Nodes and baked), export_level(), save_reproducible()
the Level class (room, vault, block, column, pipe, arch_ring, ent) and a complete reference level
re-export an edited level .blend without rebuilding it
UT99 trims (baseboards, cornices, pilasters, girders), door frame sizes (FRAMES, frame_solids) and the z-fighting check; pure Python
level scene pieces: environment, LightmapGI, probes, reflection probes, zone ambient, navigation
the scene that hosts the level glb, its lighting and probes
glb import presets: material remap onto res://materials, static lightmaps with UV2, post-import scripts
post-import: ENT_ empties become scenes, lights, triggers or markers; render extras become GeometryInstance3D settings
editor menu and BRUSHFIRE_BATCH headless nav and lightmap bakes
this skill, so the next project's agent knows the pipeline

adapt: Write game/materials/materials.json: one entry per material name with tile_m (metres per texture repeat). blendkit reads it at import and fails without it.
Put each material's textures at game/textures/<name>.png, <name>_orm.png and <name>_normal.png (optional: _emission.png) so the .blend previews them; a missing albedo gives a plain material.
Edit the SCENES and UNDERCITY maps in blender_level_import.gd to your own entity scenes; an unknown kind becomes a Marker3D in the group ent_<kind>.
Edit detailing.STYLES to your material names, and detailing.FRAMES to your door and arch props.
Edit LEVEL_MATS and the per-level entries in import_presets.py; delete the functions for assets you did not copy.
plugin.gd preloads bake_csg.gd for the CSG reference level: copy it too, or drop the csg step from the plugin.
Change the level's name, paths and lights in gen_level_blender.py, or write one generator per level from it.
